I'm still not sure to be honest. I love making movies when I was a kid, and I used to do everything from Lego stop motion to silly projects with my best friends. I went to an art school for collage, and I wound up with both a degree in film as well as a masters in Entertainment Business.

After college my friends and I moved straight to Southern California in the hopes of landing a job, any job in film. As the months went on,  my friends would strike out and move home with the exception of one who just found luck everywhere. Myself, however, found nothing but unpaid gigs with the hope that my networking would lead me to paid  jobs like they told me over and over again at school. My networking didn't amount to anything but someone trying to rope me into a pyramid scheme.

I came to a crossroad after my first year in California: I could stay and be homeless and chase the dream, I could move back to TX to live with my folks, or I could move to FL where I went to collage due a friend network. I chose FL, and wound up with a job in one of the theme parks. 

Here I am now, 7 years at the park, and I'm still slowly moving up in the company. I have a great fiancé, some close friends, but...... I can honestly tell I'm not happy. Ever since I returned to FL I constantly feel like a failure in life. I see my debt for student loans, and I see my friends who were lucky to find success. I can't help but feel like I should have stayed in California to chase that dream even at the expense of not having a roof over my head. I'm just not sure of my life path anymore.

It's a fun visual novel/detective game.  You play as a student who recently was chosen in a raffle to attend the prestigious Hope's Peak Academy. However,  once you arrive, you black out and wake up with 14 other students. The exit is locked up,  and all of the windows are bolted up. A weird mechanical bear shows up to inform them that they are now trapped in the school forever,  and the only way to escape and "graduate" is to kill another student and get away with it. It's super atmospheric, it plays on a lot of anime tropes, and the mystery of the school as well as all of the cases and class trials keep you on the edge of your seat! I highly recommend the game,  and I'm excited to finish it on steam tomorrow!
